conclusions: The failed Cocoa run races writes through the caller package-global textFieldCursor during two different window CloseReq/Scene.Close/Destroy paths. Per-window RC and Sprites locks cannot synchronize that shared pointer.
All execution modes now initialize/read/write main Scene textCursors under that main Stage Sprites lock. Deferred map write runs before deferred unlock; owner nil refuses safely under the same lock.

SpritesSource already draws cursor closures under that lock. Existing RC-to-Sprites ownership order and requestPaint-before-Sprites order are preserved; no main dispatch or new RC acquisition is introduced.
The legacy argument is ignored rather than dereferenced. Its public call signature remains source-compatible and the documentation states the changed ownership contract.

The two pinned callers only pass addresses of private textFieldCursor/lastCursor globals, with no other reads or writes relying on their updates. Cursor per-name reuse and manual-time blink behavior remain unchanged.

The map is attached to the owning main Scene and retains at most the last widget per supplied cursor name. Existing sprite closures already retain those widgets; no new process-global owner retention is introduced.
constraints: Scene/Stage topology and widget fields still require the existing originating render-context ownership; this change does not make arbitrary unsynchronized Scene deletion safe.
External users inspecting the legacy pointer will no longer receive cursor ownership updates; this deliberate behavior change is documented.
Pinned stage input/output verification, independent concurrent regression and fresh race-clean Cocoa acceptance remain separate required records.
execution: No tests, GUI, Git, Prism or shared source edits. Inert before/after snapshots and this certificate only.

historical_failure.note: Functional workflow pass precedes two race reports; it is not a native gate pass.

scope: Exact two-file prepared delta and eight selected ownership/lock/caller sources. Read-only design/API/lifetime review; not pinned patch reproduction or runtime qualification.
